Sample.evidence_source: [/page/4/Text/6] 20 cases of student suicide occurring between May 2000 and June 2005 were studied.
Sample.warning: The qualitative sample size (total_n) is not explicitly stated as a single number for participants, but rather as '73 sources of data' from '20 cases'.

Country.evidence_source: [/page/4/Text/6] All HEIs in the UK were invited to identify relevant cases for the study and 24 HEIs reported cases that met the study criteria and where staff (usually the Head of Counselling Services) felt able to assist the researchers by making the initial contact with families of students who had died. Coroners in England and Procurators Fiscal in Scotland also assisted in finding relevant cases for inclusion in the research.

Population.evidence_source: [/page/4/Text/6] All HEIs in the UK were invited to identify relevant cases for the study and 24 HEIs reported cases that met the study criteria and where staff (usually the Head of Counselling Services) felt able to assist the researchers by making the initial contact with families of students who had died. ... Wherever possible, families were approached and asked for their consent to include their son's or daughter's case in the study through an intermediary who was known to them.

Type.evidence_source: [/page/4/Text/7] Once consent had been obtained, interviews were undertaken with a parent or parents, students' friends and academic or student support staff who had known the student well. Copies of the relevant Coroners' or Procurators Fiscals' records were also acquired. Between two and six data sources were collected for each of the case studies with a total number of 73 sources of data being collated. [/page/4/Text/8] Interviews were undertaken using a semi-structured schedule and were recorded and transcribed with permission.

Area.evidence_source: [/page/5/Text/2] These key features included demographic details, details of academic route and progress, pre-university history, university context, precipitating factors and support systems.
